standard.title: Environmental Management — Environmental Performance Evaluation — Guidelines (First Revision)

sectional_committee.name: Environmental Management Sectional Committee
sectional_committee.number: EED 01 (formerly CHD 34 under the Chemical Department)

standard.description: This standard specifies guidelines for the design, development, and use of Environmental Performance Evaluation (EPE) within any organization, regardless of its size, type, location, or complexity. It defines EPE as an internal management process that uses indicators to compare an organization's actual environmental performance against its established environmental performance objectives, helping to support legal compliance, pollution prevention, and continual improvement.

certification.description: Voluntary Procedural Guidelines Standard. Unlike product specifications that govern safety-critical materials, IS 14031:2025 is a voluntary, procedural methodology standard. Organizations do not obtain a direct BIS product license or ISI mark stamp for IS 14031 itself. Instead, the standard is globally used as a technical guide to implement Clause 9.1 (Monitoring and Measurement) of ISO 14001 environmental management systems. It is universally adopted by green factories, municipal waste operations, heavy chemical processors, and ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) compliance boards to demonstrate objective, measurable evidence of their environmental performance to regulatory agencies.
requirements: Organizations must structure their EPE process based on the Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA) cycle, selecting relevant indicators, collecting and analyzing field data, evaluating performance against objectives, and reporting/communicating findings.

Organizations must track indicators that evaluate management's commitment and efforts to minimize environmental impacts. Examples include the number of achieved environmental objectives, the volume of environmental training hours completed, resources spent on pollution prevention, or the frequency of compliance audits.

Organizations must track physical indicators related to the inputs, processes, and outputs of their operations. Examples include raw materials consumed per unit of product, total energy/electricity used, hazardous waste generated, wastewater discharged, or direct greenhouse gas emissions.

Organizations must collect data describing the local, regional, national, or global state of the environment that may interact with or be affected by their activities. Examples include local river water quality (upstream and downstream of a discharge point), ambient air quality indices, soil contaminants, or biodiversity counts.
To ensure EPE reliability, monitoring and measurement devices must be calibrated or verified regularly, with all records documented and maintained for audit verification.

Establishes guidelines to share evaluation results both internally (to management and personnel to foster awareness) and externally (via corporate sustainability and ESG reports) to demonstrate policy compliance.
